requirement: Content-Length counts exactly the request content octets even when those octets contain a complete request line
notes: EchoBody consumes binary request-shaped content; a different following request is parsed and both response bodies and application paths are checked.

requirement: Chunk data and the final trailer-section CRLF delimit a request before the next message starts

RFC 9112 Section 6.3 permits 411 for a request without Content-Length; that branch does not establish chunk decoding, body drainage, or pipeline/reuse coverage. The 411 branch observes closure or a valid second response followed by closure and checks all currently published application paths for body misdispatch; partial post-411 response syntax and asynchronous future publication remain observation limits.

requirement: A request without Transfer-Encoding or Content-Length has zero content regardless of its POST method
notes: The first POST and next framed request are written together; both complete application observations distinguish the boundary.

requirement: An invalid conflicting Content-Length request requires 400 and connection closure rather than recovery at a later request line
notes: Conflicting zero/one values are the sole framing fault; a complete valid suffix is already queued. Closure follows an asserted 400 and EchoBody must receive neither request.

requirement: A request transfer coding without final chunked requires 400 and closure even when recognizable request bytes follow
notes: A valid empty gzip member follows the head before the pipelined suffix. The framing fault is missing final chunked; gzip decoding failure is not the rejection oracle.

requirement: Whitespace between a field name and colon in a request requires 400 rather than treating the framing field as absent
notes: The only syntax fault is the space after Content-Length. Explicit Connection close independently requires closure; no application observation may come from the malformed request or suffix.

requirement: A received close option prevents processing further requests after the current response
notes: This cross-reference supplies closure for the whitespace case; section 5.1 alone does not mandate closing after its 400.

requirement: A request containing Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length can be rejected or processed using Transfer-Encoding alone
notes: An accepted EchoBody response must contain the exact decoded chunk data despite Content-Length zero; rejection must produce an HTTP error response. Neither arbitrary exception nor disconnect proves success.

requirement: After either legal treatment of a request containing both framing fields the server closes the connection
notes: A complete following request is queued in the same write. Any second response bytes or second application observation fail the case.

requirement: A HEAD response ends at the header terminator despite nonzero Content-Length metadata
notes: First response declares 123 but sends no content; only after the next wire request is observed does the peer send a distinct 201 response.

requirement: Transfer-Encoding metadata in a HEAD response does not introduce a chunked body before the next response
notes: No last-chunk or trailer terminator follows the HEAD response; subsequent request/response association is checked.

requirement: A 304 response has no content even when Content-Length describes a selected representation
notes: A separate second request and 201 response expose parser state retained past the 304 boundary.

requirement: A 204 response ends at the header terminator without needing length or transfer fields or EOF
notes: The peer retains the connection and waits for the next wire request before sending its distinct response.

requirement: A status line inside Content-Length-delimited content is body data and cannot supply a later response
notes: The body includes a complete synthetic 299 response and binary octets. The second actual request must receive the separately sent 201 and its exact body.

requirement: A chunked response includes its trailer-section terminator before another response can begin
notes: Response-shaped binary chunk data ends before another request. Without TE: trailers, RFC 9112 Section 7.1.2 permits discard; retained X-Fence values must preserve their order (comma coalescing accepted). The body is asserted; the next-response boundary requires the persistence prerequisite recorded below.

requirement: When multiple requests are outstanding each response belongs to the first request that has not received a final response
notes: The authored association case uses sequential driver operations. The frozen ClientDriver cannot require pipelining two outstanding requests on a particular HTTP/1 connection; concurrent operations may legitimately use separate connections.

requirement: Data received with no outstanding request is not accepted as a valid response
notes: A convincing reuse oracle must also admit lawful connection closure and observe any replacement connection. CaseContext accepts only one connection, so a queued poison response is not used as a test that accidentally requires connection reuse.

requirement: Extra data after the completed final response to the last outstanding request is not processed as a separate response
notes: Response-shaped content inside valid framing is covered, but unsolicited bytes outside that framing require distinguishing discard, close, and later reconnect paths. The frozen one-connection client fixture does not observe all legal outcomes.

requirement: A request close option causes connection closure after the final response rather than after an interim response
notes: The frozen exchange can expose an interim ResponseData and has no continuation handle for the final response. Testing resource release alone would conflate client API lifetime with HTTP response association.

requirement: An unrecoverable response-framing error closes its connection before later requests can reuse it
notes: Direct malformed-response rejection is covered by framing cases; a complete subsequent-operation oracle must service and distinguish a lawful new connection, which this client fixture cannot do.

requirement: A client that pipelines requests can receive adjacent responses in one transport read
notes: The sequential metadata cases only send the second response after observing its request. Sending that response early would be an invalid peer stimulus unless actual client pipelining had first been established.

requirement: At the start of a new request a server ignores at least one leading empty line
notes: Direct leading-empty-line handling is covered in syntax; no interaction case yet places that line after fixed-length or chunked message completion to test parser restart state.

requirement: Generated response field values cannot insert a second response through line delimiters
notes: The authored response-shaped-body cases test recipient delimitation. Injection through untrusted application-generated header values needs a separately specified policy for pre-wire rejection versus field sanitization in the frozen Reply scenario.

requirement: An endpoint that locally resets an open stream minimally processes in-flight HEADERS to update compression state
notes: The peer-CANCEL retention case covers an entry decoded before reset. The frozen contract cannot command the target to emit a specific local RST_STREAM while proving a later field block was already in flight; cancellation/discard policy must not be assumed.

requirement: HPACK-valid field blocks still update the connection compression context when their HTTP message is rejected
notes: No case yet inserts an entry in an HTTP-malformed message and indexes it on a later stream. A legal escalation to connection termination must be recognized as an unavailable continuation prerequisite, not passed as proof of state retention.

requirement: DATA received after a local reset still consumes connection-level flow-control credit when minimally processed
notes: Reset interaction cases use small bodies and assert stream isolation; they do not saturate shared connection credit with discarded in-flight DATA or verify the ensuing credit accounting.

requirement: A zero DATA window does not prevent a legal trailer field section from completing a message
notes: The eager-window case proves PING progress and later DATA progress, not HEADERS/CONTINUATION trailer progress while DATA credit remains zero.

requirement: Lowered MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS limits new streams without requiring existing streams to be closed
notes: The two-stream peer advertises its fixed limit before requests. A later reduction while both responses are active, followed by an additional queued operation, is not covered by this fragment.

requirement: GOAWAY last-stream processing state is respected independently for streams below and above its last-stream identifier
notes: A two-stream drain/retry interaction must observe subsequent connections and replay decisions. The single accepted connection and no retry-control API prevent a complete legal-outcome oracle.

requirement: Request smuggling can arise when multiple recipients disagree on message framing
notes: This frozen baseline has one target endpoint and one scripted peer, without proxy forwarding or chained independent parsers. The covered suffix cases exercise endpoint framing consequences rather than claim end-to-end smuggling coverage.

requirement: A successful CONNECT stream transitions to tunnel DATA semantics
notes: The baseline includes CONNECT pseudo-header and framing dependencies but no tunnel application or bidirectional tunnel handle. Cross-stream tunneling and general application semantics are outside the frozen target contract.

requirement: HTTP/2 interaction fixtures preserve peer admission and advisory field-section prerequisites.
notes: Per-connection observed SETTINGS govern request admission and actual HEADERS/trailer/PUSH_PROMISE field sizes. UTF-8 wire octets plus32 per repeated occurrence are counted. Existing explicit one/two-stream and DATA-window prerequisites remain; the coalesced-preface request precedes receipt of any peer settings.
